wipe the lens at dusk, log the barges,

options: Resentful, because the narrator feels that Valentina's criticism has made her unwelcome.
Fearful, because the narrator worries that Valentina will turn Kian against her.
Dismissive, because the narrator considers Valentina's household rules trivial and outdated.
Appreciative, because the narrator recognizes care beneath Valentina's blunt manner.
g.explanation: 화자는 Valentina가 자신을 싫어한다고 말하고 빨래 개는 법과 간 맞추는 법을 지적한다고 전한다. 그러나 매일 아침 먼저 우체국에 다녀와 소식을 알려 주고, 화자의 블라우스를 수선하다 잠든 모습을 보며 무뚝뚝함 아래의 배려를 알아본다. 화자가 그녀가 선호하는 방식으로 옷을 개는 데서 존중도 드러나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 초반 인상만 본 오답이고, B와 C는 근거가 없다.

seed.topicSeed: a summer camp dining hall in the Mississippi Delta; an interpreter and her client after a misunderstood gift

g.passage:
Jamal laid the gift beside Shigeru's tray
in the dining hall of the Delta camp:
a pocketknife, worn smooth, his grandfather's.

I was the one who carried words between them,
and I chose the wrong ones, I think.
Shigeru heard keep this to cut ties
and set the knife down as if it burned.

All week the cicadas argued in the oaks.
All week the two of them ate at separate tables.

On the last night I tried again, slower,
the way you open a jar that has stuck:
keep this, so you can whittle a way back.
Shigeru turned the knife in the lamplight
and smiled the way a door opens.
g.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward her role in the misunderstanding?
options: Regretful but determined to repair the error she believes she made.
Defensive, insisting that the misunderstanding was Jamal's fault alone.
Detached, describing the conflict as though she played no part in it.
Amused by the confusion and unconcerned about its effect on the two men.
g.explanation: 화자는 통역자로서 '잘못된 말을 고른 것 같다'고 인정하며 자신의 실수를 후회한다. 이후 일주일 동안 두 사람이 따로 앉는 것을 지켜본 뒤 마지막 밤에 더 천천히 다시 통역을 시도해 오해를 바로잡는다. 따라서 후회하면서도 실수를 고치려는 A가 정답이다. B는 화자가 스스로 책임을 인정한 점과, C와 D는 그녀가 적극적으로 다시 시도한 점과 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a shopkeeper and a persistent customer
seed.conflict: about the last item in a house being emptied
seed.topicSeed: a monastery guesthouse in Manchester; a shopkeeper and a persistent customer about the last item in a house being emptied

g.passage: When the monastery guesthouse in Manchester began clearing out its rooms, I took a job helping Grant, who ran the secondhand shop that bought the contents. Most of it went quickly: iron bedframes, hymnals, a box of mismatched spoons. The last item was a plain wooden chair with one short leg, and a woman named Dana came every day for a week to ask for it. Grant refused each time. He said it was promised to a collector; later he said it was not for sale; finally he simply pretended not to hear her. I thought him stubborn, even petty. On Friday I learned that the chair had stood in the room where Dana's brother had stayed as a novice, and that Grant had been searching all week for the matching short-legged table.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Grant over the course of the passage?
options: Steady admiration, since the narrator always trusts Grant's judgment about selling items.
Initial disapproval that gives way to recognition of a motive the narrator had not seen.
Growing suspicion that Grant is hiding the chair in order to sell it at a higher price.
Lasting amusement at Grant's refusals, which the narrator treats as a running joke.
g.explanation: 화자는 Grant가 Dana의 요청을 계속 거절하자 그를 고집스럽고 옹졸하다고 여긴다. 그러나 금요일에 그 의자가 Dana의 오빠가 머물던 방의 것이며 Grant가 짝이 되는 탁자를 찾고 있었다는 사실을 알게 된다. 따라서 처음의 못마땅함이 몰랐던 동기에 대한 인식으로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 초반의 부정적 평가와, C의 의심과 D의 재미는 지문의 근거와 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a daughter and her absent father's friend
seed.conflict: about a translation that changes the meaning
seed.topicSeed: a night-shift pharmacy in Accra; a daughter and her absent father's friend about a translation that changes the meaning

g.passage: After midnight the pharmacy in Accra was nearly silent, and Adaeze worked the counter alone until Kofi arrived with the letter. He had been her father's closest friend, and he had translated the letter her father sent from Lagos years ago, the one that said he would not return. Now Kofi set the original beside her register. "I told you he chose to stay," he said. "His words were closer to 'I am not permitted to leave.' I thought that softer meaning would keep you waiting forever." Adaeze read the Yoruba lines slowly, the way she checked a prescription. For a decade she had answered his birthdays with silence. A taxi idled outside, its radio playing highlife, while a moth circled the blue sign above the door.
g.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To recount a night when Adaeze worked alone at a pharmacy until an old friend visited her.
To describe the strict procedures Adaeze follows when checking customers' prescriptions late at night.
To suggest that honesty is always the best choice, even when the truth may cause pain.
To show how learning a letter's true wording forces Adaeze to reconsider years of resentment.
g.explanation: Kofi는 아버지의 편지를 '스스로 남기로 했다'고 번역했지만 실제로는 '떠나는 것이 허락되지 않는다'는 뜻이었다고 고백한다. 이어 Adaeze가 원문을 천천히 읽고 지난 10년 동안 아버지의 생일 인사에 침묵으로 답해 왔다는 사실이 드러나, 그녀가 오랜 원망을 다시 생각하게 됨을 암시한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
